#: citare's supplement to reporters-db's reporters.json, applied by crates/citare-core/build.rs.
Each editions entry names one edition by its reporters.json key (reporter), its cluster's name, and its edition name, and replaces that edition's regexes.

Each reporters entry adds a reporter reporters-db doesn't have under its reporters.json key, as a cluster of its own with one edition; reporters-db may have the same books under another key, which then shares the slug (citare_data_build::slugs::SAME_BOOKS).
Each variations entry adds another abbreviation (variation) for one edition, named like an editions or reporters entry, that matches only through the entry's own regexes.

Each journals entry adds a secondary source journals.json doesn't have, such as an encyclopedia, to the journals under its abbreviation (edition), so a citation of it is a journal citation even when a reporter has the same abbreviation.

examples: citations the entry must recognize as that edition, with the volume each must have; rejects: citations it must no longer recognize as that edition. crates/citare-core/tests/reporters_local.rs checks both.

editions.name: Louisiana Neutral Citation
editions.notes: A neutral citation's volume is its year. reporters-db takes any volume, so it can't be told from CAP's Louisiana Reports (`la`, vols 1-263) by volume.

editions.name: North Dakota Neutral Citation
editions.notes: A neutral citation's volume is its year. reporters-db takes any volume, so it can't be told from CAP's North Dakota Reports (`nd`, vols 1-79) by volume.

editions.name: New Mexico Neutral Citation
editions.notes: A neutral citation's volume is its year. reporters-db takes any volume, so it can't be told from CAP's New Mexico Reports (`nm`, vols 1-150) by volume.

editions.name: Pennsylvania Neutral Citation
editions.notes: A neutral citation's volume is its year. reporters-db takes any volume, so it can't be told from CAP's Pennsylvania State Reports (`pa`, vols 1-639) by volume.

editions.name: South Dakota Neutral Citation
editions.notes: A neutral citation's volume is its year. reporters-db takes any volume, so it can't be told from CAP's South Dakota Reports (`sd`, vols 1-90) by volume.

editions.name: Vermont Neutral Citation
editions.notes: A neutral citation's volume is its year. reporters-db takes any volume, so it can't be told from CAP's Vermont Reports (`vt`, vols 1-203) by volume.

editions.name: Ohio Reports
editions.notes: The Ohio Reports (1821-1851) have 20 volumes, CAP's `ohio` (vols 1-20). reporters-db takes any one- to three-digit volume, so `127 Ohio 545`, the Ohio State Reports cited as `Ohio`, took the Ohio Reports' slug (#80). The variations entry below gives it to the Ohio State Reports.

editions.name: Iowa Reports, Bradford
editions.notes: Iowa's Bradford (1839-1841) has three volumes, CAP's `bradf`. reporters-db takes any volume, so `4 Bradf. 268`, Bradford's Surrogate Reports (CAP's `brad`, vols 1-4) cited as `Bradf.`, took Iowa's slug (#99). The variations entry below gives volume 4 to Bradford's Surrogate Reports.

editions.name: Caines' Reports
editions.notes: reporters-db's entry for Caines' Reports, CAP's `cai` (vols 1-3), which the reporters entry `Cai.` below adds under CAP's short name. It shares `cai` with that entry (citare_data_build::slugs::SAME_BOOKS, D78), replacing the released slug `cai-r`, which named no CAP volume. reporters-db takes any volume; this takes Caines' Reports' three, with the regexes of `Cai.`.

editions.name: Puerto Rico Reports
editions.notes: reporters-db's entry for the Puerto Rico Reports, CAP's `pr` (vols 3-100), which the reporters entry `P.R.` below adds under CAP's short name. It shares `pr` with that entry (citare_data_build::slugs::SAME_BOOKS, D78), replacing the released slug `p-r-r`, which named no CAP volume. reporters-db takes any volume; this takes the series' 100, as `P.R.` does, so `101 P.R.R. 1` is no longer a citation.

editions.name: Connecticut Superior Court Reports
editions.notes: The Reports ran 1986-1994 in a handful of volumes. reporters-db takes any volume, which also matches the Superior Court's neutral citation (`1999 Conn. Super. Ct. 13301-M`, volume a year); capping the volume at three digits lets the two share `conn-super-ct`.

editions.name: Reports of Massachusetts Appellate Division
editions.notes: The numbered series (CAP's `mass-app-div`, vols 1-15). reporters-db takes any volume, which also matches the annual series added below (`1995 Mass. App. Div. 12`, volume a year); capping the volume at three digits tells the two apart.

reporters.name: Reports of Massachusetts Appellate Division (Annual)
reporters.notes: The annual series, whose volume is its year: CAP's `mass-app-div-annual` (vols 1980-2015, 'Reports of Massachusetts Appellate Division (Annual)'). reporters-db lists only the one `Mass. App. Div.`, so without this entry a citation to an annual volume took the numbered series' slug, `mass-app-div` (#75).

reporters.name: Bradford's Surrogate Reports (N.Y.)
reporters.notes: CAP's `brad` (vols 1-4, 'Bradford's Reports'), New York Surrogate's Court decisions of 1849-1857, whose cases CAP cites as `1 Brad. 1`. reporters-db has `Brad.` only as a variation of Iowa's Bradford (`bradf`), so CAP's own citations took Iowa's slug (#99). Of the 114 `Brad.` citations in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) that CAP resolves to a case, 113 name a case in `brad` and one in `bradf`.

reporters.name: Caines' Reports
reporters.notes: CAP's `cai` (vols 1-3), Caines' Reports of the New York Supreme Court of Judicature, 1803-1805, whose cases CAP cites as `1 Cai. 1`. reporters-db has the reporter as `Cai. R.` (released as `cai-r`, now `cai`) and `Cai.` as a variation of Caines' Cases (`cai-cas`), so `1 Cai. 1` took Caines' Cases' slug (#99). Of the 117 `Cai.` citations in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) that CAP resolves to a case in either reporter, 114 name a case in `cai` and 3 in `cai-cas`; the Bluebook (T1) also gives `Cai.` to Caines' Reports and `Cai. Cas.` to Caines' Cases. reporters-db's `Cai. R.` shares `cai` (D78).

reporters.name: T.U.P. Charlton's Reports (Ga.)
reporters.notes: CAP's `charlton-rep` (vol 1, 'Charlton's Reports'), T.U.P. Charlton's reports of Georgia superior court decisions from 1805 to 1824, whose cases CAP cites as `1 Charlton Rep. 13`. reporters-db has only R.M. Charlton's reports (1811-1837, CAP's `charlton`, cited `1 Charlton 1`), with `Charlton Rep.` as one of its variations, so CAP's citations of T.U.P. Charlton took R.M. Charlton's slug (#99). Georgia opinions write `T. U. P. Charlton, 311` without a volume, which no reporter regex reads; `Charlton Rep.` is CAP's own form.

reporters.name: New Mexico Appellate Reports
reporters.notes: CAP's `nm-app` (vols 1-10, 2011-2016), which reporters-db doesn't have (#99). CAP cites every case in it by its neutral citation (`2011-NMCA-108`, `2016-NMSC-021`), and no opinion in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) cites `N.M. App.`; the edition gives CAP's slug a name and reads the citation if one is written. It takes CAP's ten volumes only: `84 N.M.App. 83` (CAP nm/84) is the New Mexico Reports with the court written into the reporter.

reporters.name: Puerto Rico Reports
reporters.notes: CAP's `pr` (vols 3-100), the English Puerto Rico Reports, whose cases CAP cites as `3 P.R. 2`. reporters-db has the reporter as `P.R.R.` (released as `p-r-r`, now `pr`) and `P.R.` as a variation of it, the Pacific Reporter and Penrose and Watts, so `45 P.R. 100` was ambiguous and took the Pacific Reporter's slug `p` (#99). All 85 `P.R.` and `P. R.` citations in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) that CAP resolves to a case name one in `pr`. Its own opinions write `P.R.R.` (30,866 times in `pr`), reporters-db's entry, which shares `pr` (D78).

variations.name: Ohio State Reports
variations.notes: Older opinions, most often Illinois and Indiana ones, cite the Ohio State Reports (1852-1964, CAP's `ohio-st`, vols 1-177) as `Ohio`. A volume of 21 to 177 can't be the Ohio Reports, which end at volume 20; of 142 such citations in CAP's case metadata for Ohio, Illinois, Indiana and Massachusetts courts and N.E.2d vols 1-250, 103 name the first page of an Ohio State Reports case and 37 a page inside one (#80). Volumes 1 to 20 stay the Ohio Reports, which they are far more often.

variations.name: Bradford's Surrogate Reports (N.Y.)
variations.notes: New York opinions cite Bradford's Surrogate Reports as `Bradf.` more often than as `Brad.`: of the 614 `Bradf.` citations in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) that CAP resolves to a case, 600 name a case in `brad` and 14 one in Iowa's `bradf`. Volumes 1 to 3 are in both reporters and stay Iowa's, the reporter reporters-db gives `Bradf.`; volume 4 is only Bradford's Surrogate Reports (69 of the 600).

journals.name: American Jurisprudence
journals.notes: reporters-db's only `Am. Jur.` is the American Jurist and Law Magazine (1829-1843, 28 volumes). Opinions after the 1930s cite American Jurisprudence, the encyclopedia (first series 1936-1948, 58 volumes), as `Am. Jur.`: `Smith v. United States ex rel. Gorlo, 7 Cir., 52 F.2d 848; 13 Am.Jur. 383` in CAP a2d/31/0693-01 (#93). Both are secondary sources, so a citation of `Am. Jur.` is a journal citation; a year in the American Jurist's run picks it, and otherwise the citation is the encyclopedia.
